rhythm.label: Thu
rhythm.slot: SAA prep (until exam) → then Udemy LLM (2h) + 30 min community

metric_defs.name: Rejection rate v2 vs v1
metric_defs.definition: Share of golden-set summaries ValidateAgainstEvidence rejects
metric_defs.how_to_measure: make eval over the frozen 30-window set; record per prompt × model

metric_defs.name: p95 latency (cached)
metric_defs.definition: 95th-percentile request latency under the standard mixed profile
metric_defs.how_to_measure: Grafana after a 10-min k6 run; never compare across different profiles

metric_defs.name: p99 latency
metric_defs.definition: 99th-percentile request latency under the standard mixed profile
metric_defs.how_to_measure: Same run as p95 — read both off one k6 pass

metric_defs.name: Cache hit rate
metric_defs.how_to_measure: Gateway cache metric over a 10-min replayed-traffic window

metric_defs.name: Cost per 1k queries
metric_defs.how_to_measure: API pricing × tokens, or GPU-hour ÷ requests served — say which in the note

metric_defs.name: Fine-tuned vs base on golden set
metric_defs.definition: Tuned ÷ base rejection rate on the golden set
metric_defs.how_to_measure: Eval runner, both providers, same day

metric_defs.name: Throughput, concurrent writers
metric_defs.definition: Messages per second with N concurrent writers on Postgres
metric_defs.how_to_measure: Rerun the W5 load profile; put N in the note

metric_defs.name: OSS PRs merged
metric_defs.definition: PRs you opened that a maintainer merged
metric_defs.how_to_measure: Count from your GitHub PR list; merged only — open or closed-unmerged do not count

metric_defs.name: Applications sent
metric_defs.how_to_measure: Count the 📮 entries in the Log for the period; the Log is the record, this is the roll-up

metric_defs.name: Medium posts
metric_defs.target: 2 by W7 · 3 by B1 · 5 by Feb
metric_defs.how_to_measure: Count live URLs; a draft is a Learned bullet, not a metric

metric_defs.name: Time to first token
metric_defs.definition: Request to first streamed token through the gateway
metric_defs.how_to_measure: TTFT metric during the standard k6 profile

goals.title: Eval harness
goals.done_means: Rejection-rate number, 30-window golden set, 2 models, CI gate

goals.title: Reliability proven
goals.done_means: RELIABILITY.md: 5 experiments w/ graphs + 1 pprof fix

goals.title: Model serving
goals.done_means: vLLM behind gateway: batching + streaming, bake-off

goals.title: Fine-tune
goals.done_means: LoRA + quantize + eval vs base on golden set

tasks.title: Golden set committed (then frozen forever)
steps: Create `eval/golden/`.
Write a tiny exporter (`cmd/goldenexport`) that dumps event windows from your dev DB to JSON, one file per window.
Pick 16–26 real windows across Energy / Finance / Monitoring.
Hand-write 4 nasty ones: `empty.json`, `single_event.json`, `one_domain_floods.json`, `same_timestamps.json`.
Add `eval/golden/README.md`: one line per file saying what it tests. Commit.
tasks.done_means: set is in git and treated as read-only from now on.

tasks.title: summary.v2 prompt in a versioned prompts dir
steps: Create `prompts/`; move the current prompt to `prompts/summary.v1.txt`.
Write `summary.v2.txt` with one deliberate change (e.g. stricter citation rules, tighter schema instructions). Note the diff in the file header.
Make `SummaryPromptVersion` load by version from that dir via config.
tasks.done_means: the pipeline runs with either version by flipping one config value.

tasks.title: OSS target picked
steps: Shortlist 3 Go projects you already use (OTel Collector, sqlc, Bubble Tea, Kafka Go client, Loki).
For each: skim CONTRIBUTING.md + the last 10 merged PRs (size, review tone, response time).
Pick one. Watch → Issues on GitHub. Bookmark 3 open issues touching code you understand.
tasks.done_means: one repo chosen, 3 candidate issues bookmarked.

tasks.title: Subscriptions + DDIA ch.1
steps: Buy O'Reilly annual + ByteByteGo. Subscribe to 2 newsletters (Pragmatic Engineer + one AI-infra).
Read DDIA ch.1; write 3 bullets in the daily log.

tasks.title: Dashboard v1 (G0)
steps: Execute `dashboard-plan.md` M0→M6 in order. Hard stop at 14h — whatever's missing goes to the stretch list.
tasks.done_means: the 6 acceptance checks pass on your phone over Tailscale.

tasks.title: Eval runner
steps: Create `cmd/evalrun`: loop {v1, v2} × {model A, model B} × every golden file.
Each run calls the existing summary pipeline; capture raw output + `ValidateAgainstEvidence` result.
Write one row per prompt×model×window to `eval/results/<date>.json`.
Add `make eval`.
tasks.done_means: `make eval` produces a committed results file.

tasks.title: Core metrics + baseline logged
steps: In the runner, compute per prompt×model: rejection rate, schema-validity % (parses as `EventSummary`), evidence-coverage %.
Print a summary table at the end of the run.
Commit the baseline results; log the headline numbers in the dashboard (📊).
tasks.done_means: baseline numbers exist in git + dashboard.

tasks.title: AWS SAA started
steps: Buy one prep course (Cantrill or Maarek — pick in 10 min, don't research for a week).
Do module 1 on Thursday; log it (📚).
tasks.done_means: module 1 logged; exam window = late Nov (book in B1).

tasks.title: Reproduce a real bug
steps: From your 3 bookmarks, pick the one you can reproduce locally.
Clone; write a minimal repro (failing test or 20-line `main.go`).
Comment on the issue with the repro + "happy to fix if maintainers agree with direction".

tasks.title: Stability + cost + latency metrics
steps: Add `-runs=N` to the runner; run each window 5× at your production temperature.
Compute drift: % of runs whose output differs field-by-field from run 1.
Record tokens + latency per call; compute € per summary from provider pricing.
tasks.done_means: results file has stability, cost, latency columns.

tasks.title: Regression gate in CI
steps: Add a `make verify` step: run eval, fail if v2 rejection rate > committed v1 baseline.
Add it as a GitHub Actions job.
Prove it: break the prompt on a branch → CI red; revert → green.
tasks.done_means: you watched CI fail on a bad prompt.

tasks.title: The sentence
steps: Fill in real numbers: "v1→v2 dropped rejection from X% to Y% on a 30-window golden set, across 2 models."
Put it at the top of the README + CV draft; log it (📊).
tasks.done_means: sentence written with real X and Y.

tasks.title: Medium #1
steps: Outline 5 sections: problem → golden set → metrics → the number → CI gate.
Draft ~1200 words Sat/Sun; include the results table + 1 diagram.
Publish; log it (✍️).

tasks.title: Prometheus + Grafana
steps: Add a `promhttp` `/metrics` endpoint.
Instrument: request-duration histogram (labels: route, provider), slots-in-use gauge, Redis-up gauge, JWKS-cache-age gauge.
docker-compose: Prometheus (scraping gateway) + Grafana.
Build one dashboard: latency p50/95/99, slots, dependency health. Export its JSON into the repo.
tasks.done_means: send test load, watch p99 move on the board.

tasks.title: OTel tracing on the hot path
steps: Add otel-go; spans for auth → ratelimit → slot acquire → provider call.
Add Jaeger to docker-compose; export traces to it.
Open one trace showing all 4 spans with timings; screenshot to `docs/`.

tasks.title: vLLM serving a small model
steps: No local GPU? Rent one (RunPod/Lambda, 24GB card, ~€0.3–0.7/h — comes out of the API-credit budget).
`pip install vllm`; `vllm serve` a small instruct model (Qwen2.5-1.5B or Llama-3.2-3B class).
`curl` the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`; confirm streamed tokens.
Save the exact launch command + model name in `docs/`.

tasks.title: PR #1 + CV line
steps: Implement the fix on a branch; add a test; follow the project's checklist (lint, commit format).
Open the PR referencing the issue. Respond to any review within 24h.
Add the eval-harness line to the CV.

tasks.title: k6 mixed-load baseline
steps: Write a k6 script (`load/`) with 2 scenarios sharing the gateway: fast client (high rps, short prompts) + slow client (low rps, long streaming), different API keys.
Run 10 min; save Grafana snapshot of p50/95/99 + error rate to `docs/reliability/baseline.png`.

tasks.title: Kill Redis mid-load (fail-open)
steps: Start mixed load; at minute 5, `docker stop redis`.
Verify requests keep succeeding; capture the degradation gauge flipping + any error blip.
`docker start redis`; verify limits re-engage.
Save annotated graph.
tasks.done_means: graph shows flat traffic through the outage.

tasks.title: Kill JWKS mid-load (fail-static)
steps: Point the gateway at a JWKS URL you control (static file server in compose).
Stop it mid-load; verify cached keys keep validating.
Verify the staleness metric is visible and rising the whole time.
Save annotated graph.

tasks.title: Slot starvation
steps: Tune the slow-client scenario to hold streaming requests until every slot is taken (slot gauge at max).
Measure the fast client during starvation: queue time, 429s, latency.
Write 5 lines: what slots showed that rate limiting alone never would.

tasks.title: vLLM wired as a provider
steps: Add a provider config entry for the vLLM OpenAI-compatible endpoint; alias it `local-small`.
Send one request through the gateway to it.
Confirm metrics/traces carry `provider=vllm`.

tasks.title: Failover lands on vLLM
steps: Priority: primary = hosted API, fallback = `local-small`.
Under load, break the primary (invalid key or null-route its host).
From traces, measure failover latency (last primary failure → first fallback success).
Assert the response names the model that actually answered.
tasks.done_means: failover latency number + model-attribution proof saved.

tasks.title: pprof: find and fix one bottleneck
steps: Under load, capture 30s CPU + heap profiles.
Pick the top hot frame in *your* code; write a one-line hypothesis.
Fix (buffer reuse, fewer allocs, avoid re-marshal — whatever the profile says).
Prove: `go test -bench` before/after + k6 p50/95/99 before/after.

tasks.title: RELIABILITY.md
steps: One section per experiment (Redis, JWKS, slots, failover, pprof): claim → method → graph → result.
Add a "what surprised me" line per section. Nothing surprised you? Re-run harder.

tasks.title: Medium #2 + honest CV numbers
steps: Post: "I chaos-tested my own README" — compress RELIABILITY.md.
Replace "~750 msg/s local" on the CV with 2–3 measured numbers (p99 under mixed load, failover latency).

tasks.title: Batching + token streaming
steps: Fire 20 concurrent requests at vLLM; record throughput vs sequential to see continuous batching work.
Verify SSE pass-through in the gateway: flush per chunk, zero buffering.
Add a TTFT (time-to-first-token) metric.
tasks.done_means: `curl -N` through the gateway streams; TTFT on the dashboard.

tasks.title: Bake-off table
steps: Pick 3–4 configs: small model FP16 · same model AWQ-quantized · hosted API model · (optional) one size up.
Run the identical k6 profile 10 min per config.
Record per config: p50/95/99, TTFT, tokens/s, € per 1k requests (GPU-hour or API price).
Commit `docs/serving-bakeoff.md`.

tasks.title: Terraform module #1: cloud Postgres
steps: Create `infra/` **inside synapsePlatform** (no fourth repo) with pinned provider versions. Neon (community provider) or RDS (official AWS provider) — pick one, don't agonize.
Write the module: instance/project, database, role; connection string as output. Secrets via variables, `.tfvars` gitignored.
`terraform apply`; connect with `psql` using the output.
Prove reproducibility: `terraform destroy && terraform apply`, connect again.
tasks.done_means: DB rebuilt from zero by two commands.

tasks.title: Postgres behind sqlc + pool + migrations
steps: Add pgx/v5 + pgxpool. Set `MaxConns` explicitly; write the justification as a comment (start: 2×cores or provider conn cap, whichever is lower).
Switch sqlc engine to postgres; regenerate; fix dialect breakage.
Init goose; schema → `001_init.sql`; wire `make migrate`.
Run the full test suite against the cloud DB.
tasks.done_means: tests green on Postgres; pool reasoning written down.

tasks.title: Follow-up
steps: PR #1 unmerged? Ping politely; offer to split or shrink it.
Bookmark issue #2 in the same repo.
tasks.done_means: PR moved or ping sent; issue #2 identified.

tasks.title: EXPLAIN → index → EXPLAIN
steps: Enable `pg_stat_statements` (available on Neon/RDS); find the slowest hot-path query.
`EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`; save output.
Add the index it asks for via a goose migration; re-run; save the after.
tasks.done_means: before/after plans committed with the timing delta.

tasks.title: Isolation level, chosen on purpose
steps: Read Read Committed vs Repeatable Read vs Serializable against your ingestion path's actual anomalies.
Set the chosen level explicitly in the ingestion transaction; write a 10-line why in docs.
Add one test demonstrating the anomaly you're preventing (or knowingly accepting).
tasks.done_means: explicit level in code + written justification + test.

tasks.title: The honest number
steps: Re-run the W5 load profile with N concurrent writers against Postgres.
Publish it in the README next to the retired 750, with one sentence of context. Log it (📊).
tasks.done_means: new number public, even if it's worse.

tasks.title: pgvector top-k
steps: `CREATE EXTENSION vector` via migration; add an embeddings column (dim = your embedding model's).
Batch-embed existing summaries through the gateway; store.
Top-k query (`ORDER BY embedding <=> $1 LIMIT k`) behind a Go function + one endpoint.
Add an HNSW index; measure query latency before/after.
tasks.done_means: endpoint returns sane neighbors; latency recorded.

tasks.title: Postgres internals reading
steps: Read: autovacuum docs, one BRIN/GIN article, partitioning overview.
Write 5 bullets: which of these synapsePlatform will need, and when.

tasks.title: Dataset curated
steps: Export input→accepted-summary pairs from your domains into `ml/data/`; target 500–2,000 examples.
Dedupe, strip anything sensitive, format to instruct JSONL; split 90/10 train/val.
Freeze val. Never train on the golden set — that's the test.

tasks.title: LoRA fine-tune → quantize
steps: Rent the same GPU class as W4; base model = the one you've been serving.
LoRA via Axolotl or Unsloth: 1–3 epochs; watch the loss curve, stop when val flattens.
Merge the adapter; quantize to AWQ (vLLM-friendly; GGUF only if you also want llama.cpp).
Save artifacts + exact configs to `ml/models/` registry notes.

tasks.title: Serve tuned model, eval vs base
steps: [gateway] `vllm serve` the tuned model; add provider `local-tuned`.
[synapse] Run the W2 eval runner: base vs tuned on the golden set (rejection, coverage, stability) + cost/latency via the bake-off harness.
Write the true verdict: "tuned = X% rejection at Y% of the cost" — whatever the numbers say.

tasks.title: SAA practice exam #1
steps: One full timed practice exam Thursday.
Log the score; list 3 weakest domains; queue those modules.

tasks.title: Checkpoint (Mon Nov 9, 45 min)
steps: In the dashboard Review, answer in writing: interview-grade eval number? chaos falsified anything? PR merged or stale? fourth repo? still AI-infra path?
Any bad answer → adjust B1 scope immediately.

tasks.title: Terraform full stack (infra/)
steps: Add a module for one small VM (Hetzner/EC2); cloud-init installs Docker + pulls your compose file (gateway, synapse services, Prometheus, Grafana).
Wire the W9 PG outputs into the app config.
`terraform destroy && apply` on a scratch env; run a smoke-test script against it.
`infra/README.md`: the one-command bring-up.
tasks.done_means: fresh environment reachable end-to-end from zero.

tasks.title: Security pass
steps: `gosec ./...` + `govulncheck ./...` on synapse, gateway, dash; fix or explicitly triage every finding.
Trufflehog scan of git history; rotate anything it finds.
30-min OWASP top-10 walk of the gateway: authz on every route, input size limits, no error leakage.

tasks.title: Polish + conference
steps: Each repo README top: what it is → the numbers → one diagram → quickstart.
Pin the 3 repos; profile README with the 3 headline numbers.
[career] Book the conference ticket.
tasks.done_means: a stranger gets the story in 2 minutes per repo; ticket booked.

tasks.title: CV + 10 applications
steps: Rewrite CV to 1 page: 3 numbers, OSS line, serving + fine-tune line.
Update LinkedIn headline; feature the 2 posts.
List 15 target companies (AI infra / LLM infra / Go platform); tailor and send 10; log each (📮).

tasks.title: Sit the SAA (G6)
steps: 1. practice exam #2 → 2. book + sit → 3. log (🎓).

tasks.title: K8s on kind (G5)
steps: 1. `kind create cluster` → 2. Deployments + Services + liveness/readiness probes in `deploy/` → 3. HPA on CPU + load until it scales.

tasks.title: Eval regression alerts (G13)
steps: 1. pick W&B (free tier) or MLflow → 2. log every eval run (params + metrics) → 3. nightly GitHub Action runs eval, alerts on regression → 4. test the alert once on purpose.

tasks.title: Medium #3
steps: the W11 table becomes "fine-tuning vs prompting, measured."

tasks.title: Udemy LLM course starts in the Thursday slot
DLQ + retries
steps: 1. create `<topic>.dlq` → 2. consumer: N retries with backoff, then publish to DLQ with error headers → 3. small CLI to inspect + replay.
tasks.done_means: a poison message lands in DLQ and replays clean.

tasks.title: Idempotency
steps: 1. event UUID + unique constraint / processed table → 2. test: duplicate delivery causes exactly one effect.

tasks.title: Backpressure
steps: 1. bound in-flight work (worker pool; pause/resume consumer on depth) → 2. slow the DB on purpose: lag grows, memory stays flat.

tasks.title: Result caching
steps: Redis cache keyed by the existing cache key, TTL configurable; hit-rate metric; tune >60% on replayed traffic.

tasks.title: Hardening
steps: timeouts on every outbound call; retry+jitter where idempotent; cost budget alert.
tasks.done_means: grep finds no call without a deadline.

tasks.title: Per-key quotas
steps: quota table + middleware + 429 with headers.

tasks.title: Udemy modules + finish DDIA + buffer. Rest counts as progress this block
Per-tenant cost dashboard
steps: tokens × price per key → Grafana panel.

tasks.title: GPU basics
steps: read one serving-GPU primer; profile vLLM GPU util during a bake-off rerun.

tasks.title: PR #2 (G7)
steps: implement → open → shepherd to merge.
tasks.done_means: merged, because one can be luck.

tasks.title: OAuth/OIDC (G15)
steps: client-credentials flow via a Keycloak container; retire static-key path behind a flag; OWASP recheck.
tasks.done_means: token-based auth works end to end.

tasks.title: Conference (G16)
steps: goal = 5 real conversations, 3 follow-ups within 48h (🤝).

tasks.title: Checkpoint Feb 21
steps: written review, same 5-question format.

Gut check, one paragraph max. Re-decide, don't re-litigate.

skills.name: Evaluation systems
skills.description: Measuring LLM output quality: golden sets, rejection/coverage/stability metrics, regression gates.
skills.associate_when: the task creates, runs, or gates on an evaluation.

skills.name: Go performance
skills.description: pprof, allocation discipline, benchmarks, hot-path fixes.
skills.associate_when: the task profiles, optimises, or benchmarks Go code.

skills.name: Load & chaos testing
skills.description: k6/vegeta, dependency-kill experiments, proving failure modes.
skills.associate_when: the task generates load, or breaks something on purpose to observe behaviour.

skills.name: Observability
skills.description: Prometheus, Grafana, OTel traces, dashboards, alerting.
skills.associate_when: the task adds or reads metrics, traces, or dashboards.

skills.name: LLM serving
skills.description: vLLM, batching, token streaming, TTFT, provider wiring, bake-offs.
skills.associate_when: the task runs, routes to, or measures a model server.

skills.name: Fine-tuning & quantization
skills.description: Dataset curation, LoRA, AWQ/GGUF, tuned-vs-base verdicts.
skills.associate_when: the task prepares data for, trains, or compresses a model.

skills.name: Postgres internals
skills.description: pgxpool, isolation levels, EXPLAIN, indexes, migrations, vacuum.
skills.associate_when: the task touches the relational layer below the ORM line.

skills.name: Retrieval & pgvector
skills.description: Embeddings, top-k search, HNSW, retrieval latency.
skills.associate_when: the task stores or queries vectors.

skills.name: Distributed systems
skills.description: DDIA theory, and Kafka in practice: DLQ, retries, backpressure, idempotency, consistency.
skills.associate_when: the task deals with partial failure between processes.

skills.name: Infrastructure as code
skills.description: Terraform modules, reproducible environments, destroy/apply proofs.
skills.associate_when: the task provisions anything by code instead of by clicking.

skills.name: Kubernetes
skills.associate_when: the task runs workloads on a cluster.

skills.name: AWS
skills.description: SAA preparation and exam, service architecture, IAM.
skills.associate_when: the task studies or applies AWS specifics.

skills.name: Security engineering
skills.associate_when: the task finds, fixes, or prevents a vulnerability class.

skills.name: Open-source collaboration
skills.description: Working in codebases you don't own: repros, PRs, review etiquette, maintainer time.
skills.associate_when: the task touches the chosen external repo.

skills.name: Technical writing
skills.description: Medium posts, RELIABILITY.md-grade docs, case studies.
skills.associate_when: the task produces prose a stranger will read.

skills.name: Career ops
skills.description: CV, LinkedIn, applications, interviews, networking, checkpoints.
skills.associate_when: the task advances the job search rather than the codebase.

skills.name: Internal tooling & DX
skills.description: Building tools that make the rest of the work faster — this dashboard included.
skills.associate_when: the task improves your own workflow with software.
